rv.q: But you don’t feel the dread in Conor McPherson’s adaptation, which seems clipped by the pace of events, all spectacle above emotion.
Yet Dunster’s production feels thuddingly perfunctory.
Transporting such a roaming, highly technical story to the stage is ambitious.
This team has staged The Hunger Games with all the bells, bangs and whistles you'd expect, but it hasn't truly understood the appeal of its source material.
And it very nearly clicks – just a stronger lead away from triumph.
Yet despite all this, though visually impressive and sometimes ingenious, the resulting show proves a curiously empty spectacle.
I’m disappointed to report that I found this unexcitingly staged spectacle an underwhelming trudge.
Unfortunately, despite its visual bravado, this production rarely hits the emotional bullseye.
